status: planned; no new Issue 14 images generated or approved
character_design: Keep approved Chano, Q and Lucía. Q has the familiar narrow segmented head, ears, long coat, worn finish, damaged shoulder and supported knee; he does not travel with Chano to administer Santa Rita. Irma remains the mayor, Leticia the cleaning organizer; Rosa is the newly named dispatcher, not motel keeper Celia. Nereida is an adult resident with the meter. Contemporary work clothes, not colonial costume.
art_direction: Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, pure white highlights and no sepia or cream ink field. Full-bleed plates at trim with separate typeset caption margin. Mexican municipal offices, a settlement clinic route and an ordinary bus station; exact-facing scenes, not generic lessons in justice. Q is remote during the route discussion. Children's drawings are drawings; the later repaired chair is not its earlier faulty state.
approval_scope: Source-bound plan only. Ten planned plates including cover, 20-page internal proof, ten A3 landscape sides / five short-edge duplex sheets. Georgia 13.3/18.8417 pt keeps the final text page substantial in both columns. No generated or approved Issue 14 assets, finished illustrated PDF or print job.

plates.caption: The Island of Good Administration
plates.scene_brief: Chano alone after closing in Santa Rita's complaint room, sunk in the five-wheel office chair until his eyes are level with stacked requests. Cracked armrest, tired but proprietary expression, no crown or throne. The chair is still municipal property. A broad quiet composition distinct from the later repair inspection and final workshop pleasure; leave space for the typeset cover title.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Fourteen: The
Island of Good
Administration
Santa Rita sent for Chano
because residents had continued
asking for him after the town
stopped employing him. The
system had classified this as
demand for a discontinued
service.
Irma's signed invitation offered a
temporary appointment with
specified authority over
emergency allocations, a budget,
and staff to receive disputed
cases. The salary was attractive.
A separate letter from Castalia
offered to withdraw its own
complaint if he accepted the
appointment. Chano sent the
second letter to the adviser and
negotiated the job without
treating it as immunity from
every other proceeding.
“They want you to make the lie
run better,” Lucía said.
“I want to make the water run.”
“They can put that in the
brochure too.”
“Then they can print it while the
truck is moving.”
Q asked whether Chano wanted
him to come. He did not. He
wanted Q to remain available for
a particular comparison of route
records if he asked for it.
“They asked for me,” Chano said.
“I don't want to arrive as your
local difficulty.”
“All right,” Q said. “I'll wait for
the request.”
“You make waiting sound busy.”
“I can put it on the list without
sending it to you every morning.”
Chano took the appointment
terms, the copies residents had
authorized him to use, and a new
notebook. His original ledger was
still retained in Tijuana. The
recovery request continued
through Elena; accepting another
job did not close that request.
Irma remained mayor. His badge
read COMMUNITY
VARIANCE OFFICER, a title
that could either authorize
exceptions or make a man
responsible for the fact that
people varied. He asked which
before signing the final terms. He
received a schedule of delegated
powers and an escalation contact.
He expected to use both.
plates.caption: They asked for me
plates.scene_brief: Before departure Chano packs a new notebook and the agreed appointment papers while Q and Lucía hear his decision to go without them. Distinguish the two letters on the table without readable legal details. Q listens rather than staging Chano as his next adventure; no original Tijuana ledger, mayoral throne or imposed knighthood.
plates.scene_anchor: Chano took the appointment terms, the copies residents had authorized him to use, and a new notebook.

plates.facing_text:
At the settlement, Maribel
showed him a temporary fence
diverting the walking route to the
clinic. A contractor had left it
around a work area after the
work was suspended. The official
alternative added a long walk to a
journey people already made
unwell.
Chano called the municipal
works supervisor. The supervisor
confirmed which section could be
reopened safely and sent a crew.
Irma approved the access
arrangement under the
temporary appointment. The
dashboard continued to display
the old route until a clerk
updated the closure.
“Which one counts?” Maribel
asked, pointing to the screen and
then the opening in the fence.
“For getting to the clinic, this
one. For making somebody pay
the crew, I'll have to finish with
that one.”
He did. The opening remained
after the first photograph of him
beside it had ceased to interest
the publicity office.
The water allocation went less
well. Chano approved an extra
tanker run to the settlement
using a roster that omitted a
recurring clinic delivery. By the
time Rosa, the dispatcher,
reached him, the driver was
unloading at the settlement.
“Where is the clinic's truck?” she
asked.
“On the extra run. There was
nothing after eleven.”
“On that screen.”
She laid the standing schedule
beside it. Chano found the clinic
entry, then his own approval on
the revised route.
“Can he go there next?”
“After refilling. I've asked him.
They need to know how late.”
He called the clinic director with
Rosa's estimate, then called again
when the refill took longer. The
residents got their water; the
clinic received its delivery late.
When he apologized, the director
asked which number she should
call next time. He gave her his
and Rosa's.
“Mine first for dispatch,” Rosa
said. “His if you need an
apology.”
Chano entered the actual arrival
time. Rosa put the standing
commitments beside the new
plates.caption: On that screen
plates.scene_brief: Rosa lays the standing tanker schedule beside Chano's incomplete digital roster as he calls the clinic with the revised estimate. Her practical insistence and his recognition of his signed approval are visible in gesture. Contemporary dispatch office, no robot present, no imagined injured patient or empty tanker magically at two sites.
plates.scene_anchor: She laid the standing schedule beside it.

plates.facing_text:
requests on the planning sheet
and made him check both.
The complaint portal yielded
thousands of entries, many
duplicates, some old, and some
urgent. He kept it open for
submissions, suspended the
automated replies that marked
cases settled without review, and
opened a room for people who
could not use it. A clerk linked
repeated entries so the same
complaint did not consume six
places in the queue. People who
disputed a link could have it
checked.
Nereida arrived with a water
meter wrapped in a dish towel. A
repair worker had replaced it
months earlier. The old serial
number still appeared on her bill,
while the new one was attached
to another property. She had
photographs, the repair receipt,
and two demands for payment.
“They asked me to bring proof,”
she said. “It was heavy.”
Chano compared the numbers
with the clerk. They requested a
correction and a hold on the
disputed charge pending review.
Nereida wanted to know whether
she could leave the meter there.
The clerk gave her an item
receipt rather than asking her to
carry it home until the office had
learned to trust a photograph.
A teacher came about a bus
diverted to another
neighborhood. She did not call its
passengers the wrong children.
They needed a bus too. She
wanted the removed service
restored without pretending a
full vehicle proved the original
route had been served.
The available options had costs:
another driver, a longer circuit,
or a changed start time that
would burden families. Chano
asked the schools and drivers to
examine them together. The first
proposal failed because it
required the same vehicle in two
places at once. No amount of
public consultation made that
arrangement more generous.
He called Q for the route
comparison they had discussed.
Q put the two versions side by
side. The revised plan no longer
required the bus in two places,
but its journey time still matched
a drive without stops.
“Has anyone timed this with the
pickups?” he asked.
plates.caption: Heavy proof
plates.scene_brief: Nereida unwraps the replaced water meter from a dish towel at the complaint-room desk. The clerk gives her an item receipt while Chano compares numbers with the two bills. Physical weight, everyday patience and bureaucratic comedy; no legible invented customer details or assertion that the charge has already been canceled.
plates.scene_anchor: Nereida arrived with a water meter wrapped in a dish towel.

plates.facing_text:
Rosa called the driver over. The
driver named three stops missing
from the line on the map. One
required a longer loop because
the bus could not turn at the end
of the lane.
“It fits if we leave those children
behind,” Chano said.
“Then we've found what made it
fit,” Q said. “Let's put them
back.”
He added the stops as the driver
described them. They checked
the new duration against the
driver's last run, and Chano
chose an interim extra trip using
the budget he controlled. The
driver asked who would pay the
additional hours. Chano entered
those before calling either school.
The permanent decision still
needed funding.
Fermín brought a notice
assigning his daughter a risk flag
after a period of absence from
school. Her mother had died. He
wanted the flag challenged, not
his daughter's grief displayed as a
case for the crowd. The clerk
received the papers privately and
explained who would review the
disputed inference. Chano asked
for a response date and an
interim limit on use of the flag
while it was contested.
The model had found a pattern.
People had decided what
consequences to attach to it.
Chano wanted those decisions
named in the answer.
Near noon the clinic director
came with another problem. A
supply delivery was delayed after
a forecasting rule reduced its
transport allowance. Lower
reported demand had been
treated as a reason to cut the
service that helped keep demand
manageable. She brought the
unfilled request and waited while
he called the transport office.
Chano confirmed the transport
needs with her and used the
emergency allocation he had
been given. The delivery reached
the clinic. He entered the request
reference and the route in the
log; in his own notebook he wrote
that an improvement could be
destroyed by deciding it no
longer needed to be maintained.
Leticia arrived with the cleaning
crew's proposed routes. The
model sent them repeatedly
through the busiest plazas and
left outlying streets waiting.
plates.caption: Put the stops back
plates.scene_brief: Rosa and the bus driver lean over the revised map beside Chano, who writes the paid additional hours. A phone on the table carries Q's remote advice, but do not depict his body in Santa Rita or invent a video call. The driver indicates a missing pickup loop; the route is a fictional municipal working sketch, not a surveyed map of real roads.
plates.scene_anchor: He added the stops as the driver described them.

plates.facing_text:
Their older schedule had
problems too.
“We can restore it for now,”
Chano said.
“And review the part we used to
complain about,” she replied.
“I was hoping to admire the old
arrangement for an entire
afternoon.”
“You can admire it while reading
page two.”
Someone brought bread. Nereida
set the wrapped meter beneath a
chair, where it would not damage
the papers. Children drew on
scrap sheets, not rejected forms
still carrying other families'
information. One gave the
dashboard a hat so it would look
as if it knew where it was going.
Chano asked whether the hat
could be issued to staff.
His first week produced real
changes and an increasing pile of
work. The dashboard's public
summary counted the restored
delivery and omitted the failed
one. It counted completed
contacts as resolved complaints.
Chano requested the categories
be separated. The software could
display them separately; the
contractor's published measure
and the ministry's reporting form
still demanded the old aggregate.
Irma arrived for the review with
the original model specification.
It gave some of the definitions
Chano had been unable to obtain
in his first appointment. Notes
from an earlier pilot warned that
lack of response could be misread
as agreement. A later
implementation had nevertheless
closed cases after a period
without replies.
“Silence is cheaper than finding
out why no one answered,”
Chano said.
“It was sold as a way to stop staff
keeping cases open for bribes,”
Irma replied.
The system had reduced some
theft and made payments easier
to trace. Residents remembered
the earlier administrations, too.
Leticia did not want cash
envelopes restored as a form of
human discretion. Fermín
wanted a human answer with a
record of who gave it. Neither
request required choosing
between the entire old system
and the entire new one.
Chano proposed publishing the
definitions and aggregate
plates.caption: A hat for the dashboard
plates.scene_brief: A child draws a hat on a picture of the dashboard using clean scrap paper while Chano asks whether staff can have one. Bread, stacked requests and Nereida's towel-wrapped meter under a chair give the room ordinary life. No real dashboard wearing a physical hat, identifiable child forms or generic protest crowd.
plates.scene_anchor: One gave the dashboard a hat so it would look as if it knew where it was going.

plates.facing_text:
correction, keeping personal case
files with the authorized
reviewers. Irma agreed to a
release of the relevant
specification pages. The
contractor objected that the
correction would invalidate the
performance claim on which its
payment depended. That
objection finally made the
meeting's attention settle on the
same number.
The next morning his account
would not open. The clerk
brought the suspension notice:
allocations and reporting under
review. Irma's signature was at
the bottom.
He found her beside the meeting
room, holding a cup whose coffee
had gone cold during a call from
the ministry.
“The contractor asked for this?”
“And the ministry. They want the
figure left alone until the
payment review. Half my
committee won't approve the
next allocation without it.”
“But that's your signature.”
“Yes.”
“You asked me to identify
errors,” Chano said.
“I expected us to agree how to
report them.”
“We did. You agreed to these
pages.”
He kept her signed release with
the specification. She did not
retract it. She asked whether the
temporary bus run would survive
until the review. He showed her
the funded dates. She copied the
last one into her diary and went
back into the meeting. His
account remained closed.
Security staff attended the
handover of keys and municipal
equipment. The police waited
outside because someone had
reported an impending
occupation. Residents were
meeting to choose who would
follow their pending cases.
Authorized contacts received
their own case receipts; the
working files stayed with the
responsible office under a
documented handover.
Chano took his personal
notebook, permitted copies, the
released specification pages, and
a list of outstanding
commitments he was allowed to
retain. The list did not authorize
him to publish every name on it.
plates.caption: Your signature
plates.scene_brief: Outside the meeting room Chano holds the suspension notice opposite Mayor Irma and her cold coffee. Her diary lies open as she checks the funded bus dates. Both are accountable adults under pressure; no evil autonomous computer issuing the notice or erasure of her earlier signed release.
plates.scene_anchor: Irma's signature was at the bottom.

plates.facing_text:
He told the residents who was to
answer next, where he could still
be reached, and what he had not
managed to do.
“Did anything work?” a journalist
asked at the gate.
“The clinic gate is open. The extra
bus is funded until the review.
Some bills are being corrected.
The reporting dispute is not
resolved.”
“Was it a success?”
“I just gave you more than one
answer.”
Q and Lucía met him at the bus
station under Q's
accompanied-visit arrangement.
He handed Lucía the public
specification extract and showed
Q the version of the route plan
the dispatcher had confirmed.
“Your second island,” Q said.
“It had mainland prices.”
“Do you want it in the book?”
“Yes. Include the tanker I sent
late.”
Q wrote that down.
“And the one that arrived on
time,” Chano added.
“Both.”
“Don't make the second one the
lesson I learned from the first.”
“I won't give the tanker a
character arc.”
“Good. It has a route.”
Q left space between the two
entries. Chano asked where they
were eating. He had spent the
journey imagining three different
lunches and wanted to know
which of them could still be
obtained.
Interlude: The Chair of
Governance
Chano did not take Santa Rita's
office chair when he left. This fact
requires stating because he spent
enough time considering it to
furnish a less scrupulous
historian with a motive, an
opportunity, and several
paragraphs of defense.
It had five wheels, a cracked
armrest, and a hydraulic column
that sank when he attempted a
particularly authoritative
posture. The chair had
introduced doubt into more
meetings than the opposition. He
grew fond of it.
During his appointment he
moved it to the complaint room
plates.caption: A route, not an arc
plates.scene_brief: At the bus station Chano shows the confirmed route plan to Q while Lucía holds the public specification extract. Q's notebook contains two separated entries; Chano turns toward the food stalls beyond them, hungry after the journey. Keep Q's known face, long coat and supported knee. No original retained ledger or files on display.
plates.scene_anchor: Q left space between the two entries.

plates.facing_text:
when somebody needed a seat
with arms. Leticia later used it at
the reception desk. The inventory
still placed it in the officer's
room. An automated audit
reported it missing.
Chano asked the clerk to change
the location. The maintenance
request attached to the chair
complicated the transfer: the
contractor was expected to
collect it from its old room. A
second employee had already
been assigned to investigate why
it was missing there.
“Can those two appointments
meet each other?” Chano asked.
The clerk called the contractor.
The older of the two men who
arrived needed to sit while his
colleague compared the labels.
Chano offered him the chair. It
sank with the dignity of an
institution accepting a reduction
in its budget.
“Column needs replacing,” the
older man said.
“That is also my assessment of
the office,” Chano replied.
The replacement part could wait
a week. The contractor could
leave the chair for seated use
with a note about the fault,
provided the municipality
accepted that arrangement. The
clerk obtained the sign-off and
corrected the collection location.
Nobody needed to pretend the
chair was inaccessible in order to
prevent its useful presence from
becoming a missing asset.
Leticia wanted it to remain at the
complaint desk after repair.
Chano wanted it back in his
office. He could explain both
desires in terms of public service.
The chair's effect on his own back
made the second explanation
especially fluent.
He called Q during their
scheduled route discussion and
asked how to record the move
without claiming authority to
give the chair away.
“You're changing its assigned use
within the municipality?” Q
asked.
“If they'll approve it.”
“Then use that request. Keep the
inventory number, proposed
room, and approver. Don't turn it
into a donation.”
“No shared-use constitution?”
“Only if the chair disputes the
room.”
plates.caption: The sinking office
plates.scene_brief: The older contractor sits in the low office chair while his colleague checks the asset label; Chano stands nearby, sharing the institutional-column joke. Cracked armrest and sagging hydraulic support visible, one intact five-wheel base. This is an authorized inspection in the complaint room, not the later repaired-chair scene.

plates.facing_text:
Chano put the phone on speaker
with the others' agreement.
Leticia said the chair had made
fewer objections than he had. Q
accepted that as the end of his
contribution and returned to the
bus timings.
Irma approved the assignment to
the complaint desk before
suspending Chano's credentials.
That left the chair where people
had been using it and deprived
him of the pleasure of taking it
away as an act of defiance. He
found this surprisingly difficult
to celebrate.
On his last evening he sat in it
after the room emptied. The
lowered seat put his eyes level
with the requests stacked on the
desk. He had liked being listened
to from the higher position. That
admission did not make the open
clinic gate false. It did make it
harder to write that he had
wanted nothing for himself.
He left the chair's inventory
number with Leticia and
returned the office keys. She
asked whether he wanted a
photograph of himself beside it.
He said no, then asked her to let
him know if the part arrived. She
promised she would.
Much later, the chair reached the
archive through a documented
surplus sale after the complaint
room obtained replacements. Its
remaining good wheel had been
exchanged with another chair;
the invoice described the
resulting collection as furniture.
Chano bought the part it still
needed and repaired it in the
workshop.
“You got the office in the end,”
Lucía said.
“Only the part that ever
supported me.”
She sat in it. It held its height.
Chano looked pleased in a way no
account of municipal
disappointment was entitled to
correct.
plates.caption: The part that supported him
plates.scene_brief: Much later in the archive workshop, Lucía sits in the repaired office chair and it holds its height. Chano stands beside his tools, openly pleased. Keep the chair's recognizable cracked armrest and repaired/mismatched parts; this follows a surplus sale, not a stolen trophy. Distinct warm composition from the cover and contractor inspection.
plates.scene_anchor: She sat in it. It held its height.
